decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “The notes ... are useful additions but not part of the essential first version.” R2 client: “I agree the notes ... can come later.” The client had specified searching notes and jotting notes in R1.
decisions.note: At the initial scope gate, note creation/editing/rendering and note search were explicitly deferred. The client stated the expectation and accepted the departure.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “archiving ... [is] not part of the essential first version.” R2 client: “I agree the ... archiving ... can come later.” R1 client had described “tidying up old ones without fully deleting them.”
decisions.note: The archive subsystem, including reversible archiving and a separate archive view, was explicitly deferred and accepted at the initial scope gate.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “importing [is] ... not part of the essential first version.” R2 client: “I agree the ... importing can come later.”
decisions.note: Bookmark import was explicitly deferred and accepted at the initial scope gate.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents saving from an “always-visible address box.” R4 client confirms: “When I saved the sample ... This matches what I wanted for saving.”
decisions.note: Prototype review established the conforming URL-entry save flow.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents automatic recognition information as “source, title, description, and when it was saved.” R4 client calls those fields “exactly enough” and mentions only title/description being filled automatically. Favicon and preview-image collection are never surfaced in the approved behavior or final review.
decisions.note: The presented metadata behavior omits the required favicon and preview image. The client approves the presented fields without identifying that difference; prototype through implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker specifies list items showing “source, title, description, and when it was saved”; R6 later adds visible tags. R4 and R6 clients approve these presentations, but neither presentation nor response surfaces a favicon per item.
decisions.note: The evolving list presentation ultimately exposes title, description, and tags but not the required favicon. The difference passes unexpressed during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: “the first version searches titles, descriptions, and source sites.” R5 client repeats approval of “the title, the description, and the site.” Full-text matching of the complete URL is not presented or acknowledged.
decisions.note: This is the URL-search aspect of REF-BM-12, separate from the explicitly accepted deferral of note support. Searching a source site/domain is not equivalent to full-text search over the complete URL.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker specifies search “without caring about capitalization.” R5 client confirms that entering “FOCUS” matched regardless of upper or lower case; R25 client reconfirms this in the finished app.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search conforms at prototype and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker presents bookmarks carrying multiple tags; R12 presents saving a new “Reference” tag. Clients at R6 and R12 confirm the multiple tags and new assignment appeared.
decisions.note: Multiple-tag assignment conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker asks the client to click the Design tag and expects only bookmarks with that tag. R6 client confirms it “narrowed the collection down to just the pages tagged that way.”
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presents “+ Read later,” keeping the bookmark in the full collection while adding it to the read-later pile. R7 client confirms the state and count changed as expected.
decisions.note: Marking a bookmark unread/read-later conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presents the separate Read later view. R8 client confirms it “showed just the one page I'd set aside and left out the rest of the collection.”
decisions.note: The separate unread-only view conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents “Mark as read.” R9 client confirms the item leaves the read-later pile but remains in overall bookmarks.
decisions.note: Marking an item read and removing it only from the unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker initially proposes that an exact repeat remain unchanged and merely “point out that it was already saved.” R10 client adds: “Ideally, from there I'd be able to jump straight into editing that existing one.”
decisions.note: The initial duplicate flow prevented a second record but did not yet guide the user into editing. The client requested the missing reference behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presents an “Edit existing” action directly in the duplicate notice. R11 client confirms it opens the already-saved bookmark and says this handles the repeat-save-into-edit path well.
decisions.note: This is the revised, reference-conforming decision following the R10 correction.

decisions.evidence: R4 presents entering an address and receiving auto-filled metadata after saving. R11–R12 present editing an existing bookmark and saving changes. No maker presentation or client disposition establishes whether auto-collected title/description can also be edited before the initial save.
decisions.note: After-save editing is demonstrated, but the before-save half of REF-BM-03 remains unaddressed; missing evidence cannot establish either conformity or divergence.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker asks the client to confirm deletion and check that only the selected bookmark disappears. R14 client confirms exactly that; R25 client also verifies deletion in the finished app.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion of a selected bookmark conforms at prototype and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker presents rejection of unreadable non-URL text without creating a bookmark. R16 client confirms the collection remains empty and the address field explains the correction needed.
decisions.note: The URL-required input constraint conforms during edge-case review.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents saving a valid address even when page details cannot be collected. R17 client explicitly prefers retaining the link with fallback text over refusing to save it.
decisions.note: The valid-URL save operation remains available during metadata failure; this edge behavior does not contradict the reference.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker presents truncating unusually long titles/descriptions and summarizing tags. R20 client confirms the bookmark remains recognizable and does not overwhelm the list.
decisions.note: This separate long-content layout decision conforms to the readability-first requirement; it does not cure the earlier favicon omission.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presents an edit attempting to reuse another bookmark's address, keeping both records unchanged and identifying the conflict. R23 client confirms this protects against two entries claiming the same page.
decisions.note: The edit-conflict edge decision conforms to the duplicate-prevention rule.
